passage: Suraj here, from the Singapore-based client team, on a video call with our Indian partners. Wasim opened with a dry joke about himself: "I'm the guy who put coffee in the printer, so trust me on the timeline." Our Dutch lead laughed. Our Japanese colleague smiled politely and looked at his notes. Later Wasim teased Kiran about being late, the way friends do in his office. Kiran said, "Ha, yes," but her camera went off for a minute. I couldn't tell whether that was the connection or the joke. At the end Wasim said, "I might keep the jokes light until I know people better," and I nodded.

qa.q: What joke did Wasim open with?
qa.a: The one about putting coffee in the printer.

qa.q: What might Kiran have felt when Wasim teased her about being late?
qa.a: Possibly uncomfortable, since her camera went off, though it could also have been a connection problem.

qa.q: What could Wasim do in mixed-culture meetings?
qa.a: He can keep humour inclusive, avoid teasing individuals and watch reactions.

qa.q: How might the Japanese colleague have understood the opening joke?
qa.a: The polite smile and looking at notes suggest they may have found it unclear or not funny, but Suraj cannot be sure; cultures use self-deprecation differently.

grounding: Jokes travel poorly across cultures, so a young professional's irony and teasing land differently with different colleagues, and he learns to keep humour inclusive.

passage:
Monday. On his first day with Aadhya's Bangalore team, Yash joked, "Sure, I love working weekends." Aadhya blinked, wrote it down and said, "Great, I'll put you on Saturday." He had meant it as irony.
Wednesday. Yash quietly said, "I was joking about weekends. I'm not free on Saturday." Aadhya laughed, embarrassed, and said, "In my last office nobody joked like that."
Following Monday. Yash opened with a light comment about the rain and asked, "Is it okay if I joke a bit? Tell me if it doesn't work." Aadhya grinned. "Rain jokes are safe."

qa.q: What did Aadhya say Yash would be put on?
What was Aadhya feeling when saying "In my last office nobody joked like that"?
qa.a: Aadhya was embarrassed, as the passage says, and perhaps a little unsure about Yash's humour.

qa.q: What did Yash change in the second week?
qa.a: He asked permission to joke and picked a safe topic, watching how Aadhya reacted.

qa.q: How might Yash have felt when Aadhya put him on Saturday?
qa.a: Yash probably felt awkward and a bit stuck, since he had meant it as irony and only corrected it quietly on Wednesday. 🙂

grounding: Irony that suits one workplace can be taken literally in another, so a young professional adjusts his humour and checks reactions.
